rows.32:0954:
...I see.
That's a safe answer.
They say people who answer like that secretly think they're pretty cool, deep down.
I'm sorry for asking you something so strange.
May I ask you one more strange thing?{p}
rows.32:0a60:
...So you hate rain.
I love it.
The rainy season most of all.
When the hydrangeas bloom.
The air is so humid that its lukewarm touch soaks right into your skin.
My shirt clings wetly to my skin and doesn't even stir in the wind, and it makes me truly feel that I'm wearing clothes. I find that so lovely.
And in the rainy season, it could start raining at any moment, couldn't it?
Weather that threatens rain but never brings it.
A sun shower, when rain suddenly pours from a cloudless blue sky.
Rain sends shivers of delight through me.
I'd like to live in a world where the rain never stops.
Sometimes the thought just comes over me.{p}
rows.32:0c78: Tell me, {a}, when it rains, do you use an umbrella?{p}Or do you like to go without one and get soaked?
rows.32:0cf8: It depends on how hard it's raining
rows.32:0d18:
Oh, I see.
What a waste of lovely rain.
Rain is a blessing from heaven.
God goes to the trouble of sending it down just for us, and yet...
I never use an umbrella.
Never, no matter how hard it pours.{p}
rows.32:0de8:
I take in a whole sky full of rain and turn my face up to the heavens.
And I catch the rain with my whole body.
It's wonderful.
Because it feels so good.
You should try it once yourself.
When the rain is light, it turns into a mist that tickles my skin and makes me feel it.
When the rain is heavy, it beats down hard on my body with a fierce roar.
The rain is alive.{p}
rows.32:0f38:
Heh heh... Maybe you can't understand this pleasure.
But the story I'm about to tell may be just perfect for someone like you, who hates rain and shuts out lovely rain with an umbrella.{p}By the way, {a}, do you keep a spare umbrella at school?
rows.32:1050:
Of course.
I think that's how most people who use umbrellas are.
Especially in the rainy season.
Even if you keep a spare umbrella at school, when it suddenly starts raining, you end up using it, don't you?
And then, when the next day is sunny, it seems people just forget to bring an umbrella back.
Not many people keep three or four spare umbrellas at school.
If anyone did, they'd simply be lazy, wouldn't they?
So in the rainy season, rain or shine, you'd have to carry an umbrella every single day.
But that's not easy to do.
Umbrellas are such a nuisance.
When it looks like it couldn't possibly rain, hardly anyone walks around carrying an umbrella, right?
And even if they do, they'll just end up leaving it somewhere.
That's why in the rainy season, you often see people waiting out the rain by the shoe lockers.{p}
rows.32:1330:
How stupid of them.
It's lovely rain, so they should just get soaked to the skin on the way home.
People clicking their tongues, looking up at the sky with openly disgusted faces, as if they hated heaven itself...
I can't understand people like that.
People like that ought to just die.
{a}, you're not that kind of person, are you?
...Hehehe.
They're just awful, people who wait out the rain.{p}
rows.32:147c: But you know, for a girl, it's also the perfect chance at love.{p}
rows.32:1558:
Once, there was a girl named Yukari Tachibana.
She was in love with someone.
His name was Hiroshi Tsukahara.
Tachibana was by no means an unattractive girl.
If anything, she was cute.
But she wasn't the kind of flower that stands out from all the rest.{p}
rows.32:1654:
Tsukahara, on the other hand, was incredibly good-looking.
He had features that hardly looked Japanese, a fine, chiseled face, just like a model.
Mind you, I never actually saw either of them, so I don't know what they looked like.
So of course he was popular.
He always had a following of girls around him, squealing over him.
Frankly, Tsukahara didn't have a very nice personality.
He took it for granted that girls would fall for him, and he acted like a star.
So the other boys hated him.
But Tsukahara didn't care about that. If anything, it gave him a sense of superiority, and it went straight to his head.
Honestly, he was a nasty piece of work.{p}
rows.32:1978:
It was the rainy season, and Tsukahara had no umbrella, so he was waiting out the rain.
The very situation I just described.
At that moment, by chance, none of his followers were around.
And Tachibana had an umbrella.
A big red umbrella.{p}
rows.32:1af8:
"...Um, are you waiting for someone?"
"Nah, not really.
It started raining, so I've got no choice but to wait it out.
I don't want my hair getting wet.
Man, what a pain. Stupid sky."
With that, he glared up and cursed the sky, as if he hated heaven itself.
"...Um, here.
Would you like to share it with me?"
Tachibana held out her red umbrella.
"Oh, yeah?
Thanks.
You're a lifesaver.
Which way are you headed?"
Shameless as he was, Tsukahara was never going to turn down an offer like that.
"...Um, which way are you going, Tsukahara?"
"Huh? You know my name?
Wow, I'm flattered.
Oh, my place is that way."
The direction Tsukahara pointed was the opposite way from the station Tachibana was heading for.
"Oh, me too."
But Tachibana said it with a smile.
It was her big chance, after all.
A little lie like that didn't bother her at all.{p}
rows.32:1e14:
And so the two of them walked shoulder to shoulder under one umbrella.
Tachibana was so happy.
She wished time would just stop right there.
She even thought that as long as this happiness lasted, she didn't care what became of her.
"So, what's your name?"
"It's Yukari Tachibana."
"Oh, Yukari.
Hey, Yukari, have we met somewhere?"
"...No. I think this is the first time."
"Huh. And you still knew who I was.
How come?"
That's just the kind of person Tsukahara was.
If it had been me, I might have killed him.
But Tachibana was an earnest girl, you see.
"...Oh, well, I've been a fan of yours, Tsukahara."
"Wow, that makes me happy.
Thanks."{p}
rows.32:2068:
With that, Tsukahara put his arm around Tachibana's shoulder and pulled her close.
For Tsukahara too, a girl like her was something rare.
Most of the girls around him were the pushy type who squealed over him, after all.
So a girl like Tachibana seemed fresh to him.
"You're really cute, Yukari.
I wouldn't mind making you my girlfriend."
Of course, he was only half serious.
It was a line he said to every girl, without a second thought.
But to her, it was different.
Tachibana's heart was ready to leap out of her chest.
She was so happy, so very happy, she thought she might lose her mind.
And she prayed that this wasn't a dream, and said thank you to God.{p}
rows.32:22c0:
"If you want, why don't you come over to my place now?
I want to get to know you better, Yukari, and I think we'd really hit it off."
Tachibana was never going to say no.
She accepted his invitation in a heartbeat.
The Devil's invitation.{p}
rows.32:23a0:
Tell me, {a}.
What do you think of this guy Tsukahara?{p}Maybe he's a lot like you, hmm?
rows.32:2404: He's a guy I can't stand
rows.32:2430: I'd rather not get involved in other people's business
rows.32:24c0:
Tachibana went along with Tsukahara.
And she went into his house.
His parents weren't home.
Well, he knew that, which is why he lured her there, I suppose.{p}
rows.32:257c:
She was a butterfly caught in a spider's web, wasn't she?
Even if she'd tried to escape, he would never have let her go.
But Tachibana had no need to escape.
She never even thought of escaping.
Because she was happy too.
Being alone with Tsukahara... there was no greater happiness for her.
Tachibana already did whatever Tsukahara told her.{p}
rows.32:26cc:
Those were truly happy days.
At school too, she stuck to Tsukahara's side.
But his followers didn't get angry, and they didn't complain to Tachibana either.
They just watched from a distance, sneering.
As if they already knew how it would end.{p}
rows.32:27d0:
And that end came soon enough.
It took Tsukahara less than a week to get bored of Tachibana.
In the end, he probably just couldn't get along with a serious, boring girl who did nothing but whatever he said.
Tachibana was dumped, just like that.
Tachibana didn't understand what had happened.
She couldn't grasp where she stood right away.{p}
rows.32:2934:
After all, Tsukahara had suddenly turned cold toward her.
More than cold, he ignored her, or rather, he started looking at her as if she were something filthy.{p}
rows.32:29d4:
On the surface, he kept up appearances and smiled, but Tachibana loved him, and she could read his heart like an open book.
'You're in my way. Hurry up and get out of my sight.' That's what it said.
Tachibana was earnest, and he was the first boy she had ever gone out with.
So she couldn't understand why he had changed so suddenly.
He wouldn't answer her calls, and when they met at school, he wouldn't even speak to her.
He'd trade a few smooth words with her, then go straight off to the other girls.{p}
rows.32:2b70:
Still, as time went by, she came to face the truth: she had been dumped.
She had only been toyed with.
But she couldn't forget Tsukahara.
That's how much she loved him.
And she made herself believe that the week they spent together had been a dream, a gift from God.{p}
rows.32:2cac:
And so she went back to watching him from afar.
That way, she wouldn't get in his way, and he wouldn't come to hate her.{p}
rows.32:2d30: ...Tell me, {a}.{p}What do you think of Tachibana, being like that?
rows.32:2d84: I think she's a bit odd
rows.32:2e34:
...Thank you for answering my question.
I'm sorry. I'll go on with the story.{p}
rows.32:2e9c:
But God does love his little pranks, doesn't he?
After all, he gave Tachibana one more chance.
It was toward the end of the rainy season.
Maybe Tsukahara just isn't the type to keep a spare umbrella at school.
He was waiting out the rain again.
All by himself.
And Tachibana had an umbrella.
A big blue umbrella.{p}
